messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: PROD cluster decode-prod-us-west-2 has sustained p99 decode latency spike. p99 jumped from ~2.1s to 7.3s starting at 2026-03-15T13:58:12Z. Affected route: /v1/decode (streaming). Suspected correlated deploy: runtime-kernel v2.14.0 -> see dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/alerts/3265

maya (oncall): ack. paging oncall. I'm looking at traces and realtime p95/p99. Any recent deploys or rollout notes?

ops-bot: deploy-log: runtime-kernel v2.14.0 rolled to canary (40%) at 2026-03-15T13:45:03Z via release/rt-2.14.0. No auto-rollback triggered.

alex (runtime): I saw the metric bump correlated with the canary window. v2.14.0 bundles TRT8 kernel updates + FlashAttn patch and a different compile flag set (LTO enabled). Early suspicion: new kernel + compiler flags causing worse tail behavior for decode path (KV caching + streaming interactions).

sam (sre): checking infra. Noticed increased GPU memory pressure and >0.5% OOMs on affected pods; also more host-level swap activity on ~6 nodes. Paging/evictions visible in node logs.

jordan (eng): we enabled fused-attention path on TRT8 in this build; that path reduces avg latency but has worse worst-case for long context with KV cache churn.

maya (oncall): immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback canary to v2.13.9 on a subset, 2) change routing to avoid canary nodes, 3) disable fused-attention via runtime env override, 4) scale up capacity. Which is fastest?

alex (runtime): fastest is rollback the canary portion -> we have rollout groups. Command: 

```bash
# roll canary back to 2.13.9 for runtime-kernel deployment group rg-canary-usw2
kubectl -n runtime set image deploy/runtime-kernel runtime-kernel=redwood/runtime-kernel:2.13.9 --record 
# or use release manager: redwoodctl rollout undo --group rg-canary-usw2 --to-version 2.13.9
```

alex (runtime): alternative quick hotpatch: set env RUNTIME_FORCE_LEGACY_ATTENTION=1 on canary nodes (no rebuild). That flips off fused path.

maya (oncall): starting rollback on canary now (rg-canary-usw2). I'll monitor p95/p99, streaming stalls, and metrics.

ops-bot: rollback started at 2026-03-15T14:02:20Z by maya. Progress: 0/40 nodes completed.

maya (oncall): update: 12/40 nodes rolled back. p99 dropping on those nodes from 7.3s -> ~2.4s. Overall p99 across cluster now 4.8s and trending down. Some dedicated customers still seeing tail spikes because they route to pinned nodes that haven't been rolled.

sam (sre): for pinned/dedicated hosts we should consider runtime routing change: route traffic away from nodes with runtime-kernel v2.14.0. I can push a routing policy that prefers nodes tagged kernel=v2.13.9.

jordan (eng): long-term: we should revert the fused-attn default until we can add guardrails for long-context KV behavior. I'll open a PR to change default in next RC. For now we can ship a kernel build with the fused flag off.

maya (oncall): customer impact: we flagged 3 customers (acme-corp, fincorp, learnify) who reported >30% p95 regression and some streaming stalls. I've notified CSM and support to prepare incident emails. Marking SEV2 for now.

devops-bot: incident created PD-4883 (SEV2) at 2026-03-15T14:05:10Z. Incident doc: https://incidents.redwood.internal/PD-4883

maya (oncall): current state at 14:12 UTC: canary rollback 75% done, cluster p99 ~2.3s, p95 ~1.1s but streaming tail still has intermittent stalls. Actions so far: rolled canary, routed traffic off worst nodes, notified customers, escalated to eng-runtime + SRE.

alex (runtime): next steps for runtime: 1) complete global rollback if metrics stabilize, 2) otherwise build hotfix v2.14.1 with fused-attn off and compiler flags reverted (disable LTO), 3) prepare alpha test on a small set with heavy long-context load.

sam (sre): also watch for KV cache thrash logs: sample log snippet below where eviction count spikes during a single request: 

```
2026-03-15T13:59:45Z [decode-worker] kv_cache_evictions=124 evicted_pages=3 peak_mem=18.7G
2026-03-15T14:00:12Z [decode-worker] kv_cache_evictions=312 evicted_pages=9 peak_mem=19.9G
```

maya (oncall): note for handoff in 40m: if rollback stabilizes (p99 < 2.5s for 15m), we can close incident with postmortem. If tail persists, we need global rollback + targeted hotfix. Handoff checklist: links, commands executed, logs to keep, customer list, route to disable fused-attn env if needed.

alex (runtime): relevant commands and runbook snippets: 

```
# force legacy attention on a node (no deploy):
kubectl -n runtime set env ds/runtime-worker RUNTIME_FORCE_LEGACY_ATTENTION=1 --selector=kernel=2.14.0-canary

# routing policy to avoid canary-tagged nodes:
redwoodctl route set --service decode --avoid-tag kernel=2.14.0-canary --region us-west-2
```

maya (oncall): I'm going to expand rollback to all canary nodes now that p99 improvement is consistent. Handing off in 40m to alex (overnight). Leaving notes in PD-4883. Any objections?

jordan (eng): no objections. I'll pause fused-attn rollout and open PR for flag default change.

sam (sre): I'll keep watch on host swap and eviction metrics, prepare to reimage nodes if memory-corruption symptoms appear.

maya (oncall): handoff: alex (runtime) you own the incident from 14:52 UTC -> please continue rollout, verify p99/p95 for 30m post-global-rollback, coordinate with support for customer follow-ups, and start postmortem draft. Key artifacts: PD-4883, rollback command logs, perf traces, and a sample failing request trace (attached in PD).

alex (runtime): ack. I'll take it and update PD-4883 and the #eng-runtime channel. If we see remaining p99 >3s after global rollback I'll trigger build of v2.14.1 (disable fused, revert LTO) and run small canary alpha with synthetic long-context load to validate.

ops-bot: handoff logged. Next-oncall: alex (runtime).

maya (oncall): thanks team. Closing immediate paging loop; keep this thread for notes and the postmortem. :white_check_mark:
